key_insight: Single success metrics hide critical operational flaws; building a "science of AI agent reliability" requires multidimensional evaluation that measures consistency, robustness, failure predictability, and bounded error severity.
problem_solved: Bridges the gap between benchmark accuracy and real-world agent failures by providing a framework and metrics to reveal and quantify when and how agents fail across runs and perturbations.
method: Define concrete reliability dimensions and metrics (consistency across runs, robustness to input/ENV perturbations, predictability of failures, and error-severity bounds).
Design evaluation protocols: multi-run analyses, systematic perturbation/stress tests, and failure-mode logging to surface latent weaknesses.
Apply metrics to agents to characterize trade-offs, expose repeatable failure modes, and support comparative reliability profiling.
impact: Gives ML practitioners actionable diagnostics beyond a single score—enabling safer deployment, targeted fixes, and more reliable monitoring of agent behavior in production.
visual_elements: Radar (spider) chart showing an agent's scores across the reliability dimensions (consistency, robustness, predictability, severity).
Line chart of performance vs. perturbation strength (robustness curve) to show degradation under stress.
Stacked bar or waterfall chart of error-severity distribution to emphasize boundedness and rare catastrophic failures.
Heatmap/matrix of failure modes across runs and tasks to highlight repeatable vs. stochastic failures.
paper_title: Towards a Science of AI Agent Reliability
paper_authors: Stephan Rabanser, Sayash Kapoor, Peter Kirgis, Kangheng Liu, Saiteja Utpala
